# google_network_connectivity_interconnect_key_group

An InterconnectKeyGroup holds a set of customer-provided MACsec keys (CKN/CAK pairs) that one or
more Cloud Interconnect connections can use for MACsec ("bring your own key"). Link an
Interconnect to a key group with the `macsec.interconnect_key_group` field of
`google_compute_interconnect`.

Individual keys can't be changed in place. To rotate keys, add a new key (with a `start_time`
at least 6 hours in the future) and remove the old key once the new key is active. Keys can be
added and removed while the key group is attached to Interconnects; the changes are pushed to
every linked Interconnect without disabling MACsec.

~> **Warning:** This resource is in beta, and should be used with the terraform-provider-google-beta provider.
See [Provider Versions](../guides/provider_versions.html.markdown) for more details on beta resources.

To get more information about InterconnectKeyGroup, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/reference/networkconnectivity/rest/v1beta/projects.locations.interconnectKeyGroups)
* How-to Guides
    * [MACsec for Cloud Interconnect](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/macsec-overview)

~> **Warning:** `keys.cak_wo` is a write-only argument and requires Terraform 1.11 or later. The CAK is never
stored in Terraform state or plan files, and the API never returns it.

~> **Note:**  All arguments marked as write-only values will not be stored in the state: `keys.cak_wo`.
[Read more about Write-only Arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/write-only-arguments).

## Example Usage - Network Connectivity Interconnect Key Group Basic


```hcl
resource "google_network_connectivity_interconnect_key_group" "default" {
  provider    = google-beta
  name        = "my-key-group"
  region      = "us-east4"
  description = "MACsec keys for my Interconnects"
  labels = {
    env = "test"
  }

  keys {
    name       = "key1"
    start_time = "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    ckn        = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
    # Write-only (Terraform 1.11+): sent to the API but never stored in state or plan files.
    # In real configurations, pass this from an ephemeral variable or ephemeral resource.
    cak_wo     = "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `region` -
  (Required)
  The region of the key group. Only Interconnects in this region can use it.

* `name` -
  (Required)
  The name of the key group.


* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  Labels as key-value pairs.

  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  An optional description of the key group.

* `keys` -
  (Optional)
  The MACsec keys in this group. A key group can have at most 5 keys, and the start times of
  any two keys must be at least 6 hours apart. When the key group is created, keys can have a
  `start_time` in the past; keys added later must start at least 6 hours in the future.
  The order of the keys doesn't matter. Keys can't be changed in place: to change a key, add a
  key with a new name and remove the old one.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_keys).

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_keys"></a>The `keys` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  A name for this key, unique within the key group: 1-255 lowercase letters and digits.
  The API only accepts alphanumeric names; uppercase letters aren't allowed because the
  provider uses the name as an update-mask path (`keys.<name>`), and mask paths are
  case-converted.

* `start_time` -
  (Required)
  The RFC3339 timestamp from which this key takes effect, for example
  `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`.

* `ckn` -
  (Required)
  The MACsec connectivity association key name (CKN): a 64-character hexadecimal string.

* `cak_wo` -
  (Optional, Write-Only)
  The MACsec connectivity association key (CAK): a 64-character hexadecimal string.
  Write-only (requires Terraform 1.11 or later): it is sent to the API but never stored in
  state or plan files, and the API never returns it. Required for every key that is being
  added. Changing only `cak_wo` of an existing key has no effect; to change a CAK, add a
  new key and remove the old one.
  **Note**: This property is write-only and will not be read from the API.

  ~> **Note:** One of `cak` or `cak_wo` can only be set.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/interconnectKeyGroups/{{name}}`

* `create_time` -
  The time the key group was created.

* `update_time` -
  The time the key group was last updated.

* `interconnects` -
  The names of the Interconnects that use this key group.

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 30 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


InterconnectKeyGroup can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/interconnectKeyGroups/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{name}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import InterconnectKeyGroup using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    region = "<-required value->"
    name = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_network_connectivity_interconnect_key_group.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import InterconnectKeyGroup using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/interconnectKeyGroups/{{name}}"
  to = google_network_connectivity_interconnect_key_group.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), InterconnectKeyGroup can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_network_connectivity_interconnect_key_group.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/interconnectKeyGroups/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_network_connectivity_interconnect_key_group.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_network_connectivity_interconnect_key_group.default {{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_network_connectivity_interconnect_key_group.default {{name}}
```
